versions.name: RXV2-0.9.768-ticked-lane-runs
versions.notes: Update page: the lane shown ticked is the one the install uses - with no WiFi up, Bluetooth starts at once instead of waiting 45 s for WiFi first.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.767-wire-finder
versions.notes: Simulator interface: while nothing is recognised, the dongle counts signal edges on D4, D5 and D6 and the dongle page names the pad the wire is really on.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.766-wire-raw-and-sbus-ni
versions.notes: Simulator interface: while a signal is arriving but not recognised, the dongle page shows what each protocol saw and the last bytes raw; and SBUS on a non-inverted line is now recognised too.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.765-background-drop-guard
versions.notes: Apps: with Bluetooth now running in the background, a link the receiver drops while the app is in the background (its idle watchdog, nothing installing) is no longer chased - that would have reconnected, gone silent and been dropped again every few minutes. Installs still ride out the reboot.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.764-no-radio-warning-on-sim-if
versions.notes: Front page: no 'No transceivers detected' warning on a board in the Simulator interface role - it has none by design, like a dongle.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.763-install-survives-lock
versions.notes: A Bluetooth install now carries on when the phone's screen locks or you switch to another app: the iPhone keeps Bluetooth running in the background, Android runs the install under a foreground service, and both hold the screen awake while it runs.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.762-wire-diag-and-role
versions.notes: Dongle page: one plain choice on a board with no transceivers - Rotorflight dongle or Simulator interface - and nothing to choose on a receiver. The simulator interface says what it hears on D5 (nothing, unrecognised, or locked) and logs locks and losses. Bluetooth installs: the apps now wait four minutes for the receiver to come back, and return to the list instead of reloading over a link that is not back.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.761-mode-row-and-lane
versions.notes: Two things Malcolm met while testing the dongle. FIRST: 'there was no mention of simulator mode'. Quite so - the Mode row was hidden on a dongle, because until this week the board worked out for itself what it was and there was nothing to choose. Now there is a third role, Simulator interface, and it was invisible on the very page that offers it. A board with no radio now always shows the Mode row, since it can be either role. SECOND: 'even though Bluetooth is selected, it's attempting to download over Wi-Fi and failing'. The install waited up to 45 seconds for the receiver's WiFi to come up before starting, whatever lane had been chosen - so choosing Bluetooth meant waiting three quarters of a minute and then using Bluetooth anyway. Tapping Bluetooth now means Bluetooth at once. Pages only.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.760-wifi-button-always
versions.notes: Two faults from one afternoon, both worth having found. FIRST, and much the more serious: a filesystem update that did not finish left the board crashing on every boot, for ever, recoverable only by a USB reflash - which is exactly what happened to Malcolm's dongle after an over-the-air update at -83 dBm. The recovery code wiped the half-written pages BEFORE mounting the filesystem, and the library only learns which partition to wipe when it mounts, so it wiped nothing and crashed instead. It now mounts first. Any board, receiver or dongle, could have been stopped this way by a power cut or a weak signal during the pages part of an update. SECOND: the WiFi button was shown only when WiFi or the access point was already up. In the app, where the page arrives over Bluetooth, that is a catch-22 - the one moment you need the WiFi settings is when WiFi is not working (wrong password, a new router, a board carried to a different house). In the app the button is now always there; in a browser it still depends on an interface being up to serve the page at all, which is simply true.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.759-simif-status
versions.notes: The Simulator interface role could not show itself: the status flag went into the 'fcinfo' part of the receiver's state, and the dongle page looks for it at the top level beside the dongle flag (found on Malcolm's DongleSim board, 2026-09-18). So the Mode card never displayed the role, its wiring note, or whether a receiver had been found on the wire. Moved to where the page looks. Everything else about the role was correct. Pages and one status line.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.758-sim-roles-clear
versions.notes: Making the two simulator routes plain (Malcolm 2026-09-18: 'a receiver with transceivers should STILL be able to operate in Simulator mode! It's even simpler for use as a receiver is built in'). He is quite right, and it always could - the receiver's own Simulator mode was never touched by yesterday's new role and needs no wire and no second board: a receiver plugs straight into the computer and flies the simulator from your own transmitter. What was wrong was the dongle page, which offered a board with its own radio the wire-fed Simulator interface role and then refused it. That option is now simply not offered to a board with transceivers, and the page says where its own Simulator mode lives instead. Pages only.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.757-simulator-interface
versions.notes: The dongle gains a third role: Simulator interface (Malcolm 2026-09-17: 'all we need to do is add to the dongle a new option called Simulator interface'). A board with no radio, with one of your receivers wired to it, becomes a USB joystick for a simulator on the computer - Windows or Mac. Wiring is the same four-wire lead with the flight-controller end moved to the receiver: the receiver's signal output to D5, its 5 V to the board's 5V pin, ground to ground; then a USB cable to the computer, which powers the whole rig. No battery, no flight controller. CRSF, SBUS, IBUS and PPM are recognised on their own, and the Mode card says which was found and how many channels arrived. Everything else - which stick drives which axis, reversing, the spool-up realism, the camera keys - is on the Simulator pages exactly as it has always been, because the decoded channels are put precisely where the radio would have put them. This retires the separate LDRC2SIM firmware: one board, one firmware, three roles. A board with transceivers fitted is refused this role, because it belongs in a helicopter. Nothing changes for a receiver or a Rotorflight dongle.

rotorflight.line: Rotorflight 2.3 — the release these pages are written and tested against.
